title: IES 89 12 corn (IES Var 89 12): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: IES 89 12 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: IES 89 12 corn is a white open pollinated corn variety for Luzon. 97 to 105 days to harvest, 5.5 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: IES 89 12 corn is a white open pollinated corn variety, also sold or known as IES Var 89 12. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Cn 187. CVIARC bred it. It takes 97 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 5.48 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 97 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 5.48 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** Luzon, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.caption: Key facts of IES 89 12
rows: Both the wet and the dry season

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

IES 89 12 corn takes 97 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 28 white open pollinated corn varieties with a day count, 103 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 5.48 t/ha matches the average of its group, 5.36. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 95 to 100, 97 to 105 in NSIC trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its ears grew about 15.35 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 74 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears. Against lodging it rated resistant, so it stood up well when wind and rain pushed the plants.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: Rated resistant to corn borer, earworm and leaf diseases in the DA Region 2 guide.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: among the three white corns Isabela farmers liked best in the 2011 to 2013 farmer trials, on DA Region 2's recommended list. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant IES 89 12 corn

It is recommended for Luzon in both the wet and the dry season. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is IES Var 89 12 the same as IES 89 12?
items.a: Yes. IES Var 89 12 is another name for IES 89 12, registered as NSIC 2006 Cn 187. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 97 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.48 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.
It is recommended for Luzon in both the wet and the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of IES 89 12?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
